attractions.name: Makli Necropolis
attractions.description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the largest funerary sites in the world, with hundreds of thousands of tombs spanning several centuries.

attractions.name: Shah Jahan Mosque
attractions.description: A 17th-century Mughal-era mosque famous for its intricate tile work, built during the reign of Emperor Shah Jahan.

attractions.name: Keenjhar Lake
attractions.description: One of the largest freshwater lakes in Pakistan, popular for boating and picnics, and an important bird habitat.

transportation.notes: Regular daily departures, easy day trip from Karachi
Round-trip fare typical for the lake visit

seasonal_notes.avg_condition: Mild, 14-26°C, ideal for visiting Makli and Keenjhar Lake
Coastal weather systems can bring periodic rain

travel_tips.tip: Thatta is an easy day trip from Karachi, well connected by a direct highway.
Combine a Makli Necropolis visit with Keenjhar Lake and the Shah Jahan Mosque in a single day trip, all relatively close together.
Wear comfortable shoes for walking around the extensive, uneven terrain of the Makli Necropolis.
Visit Makli Necropolis in the morning to avoid the afternoon heat, since much of the site is exposed with little shade.

history.founded: An ancient city with a history spanning over a thousand years, once a major center of learning and trade
history.city_history: Thatta served as the capital of Sindh under several dynasties and was once described by travelers as one of the greatest cities in the Islamic world, with hundreds of schools and a thriving textile trade. Today it's best known for the Makli Necropolis, one of the largest burial sites in the world, and the beautifully tiled Shah Jahan Mosque.
history.province_history: Sindh is home to one of the world's oldest urban civilizations, the Indus Valley Civilization (Mohenjo-daro), and was later ruled by Persian, Arab, and Mughal empires, as well as the Talpur dynasty, before British annexation in 1843 and eventual inclusion in Pakistan in 1947.
